about.intro_content: Prof. Zhong-Ping Chen is Professor and Founder Chairman of the Department of Neurosurgery/Neuro-Oncology at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou, and Founder President of the Chinese Society of Neuro-Oncology (CSNO).
about.detailed_content: Prof. Chen's clinical interests include microsurgery and multimodality treatment for primary and metastatic central nervous system tumours, particularly gliomas, with chemotherapy and immunotherapy as important adjuvant treatments. He was the first to identify vasculogenic mimicry, a novel form of circulation in malignant gliomas, and has investigated immunotherapy approaches including CIK cell local therapy and dendritic cell-glioma fusion cells. Over the past 20 years he has participated in more than 20 glioma treatment clinical trials as Principal Investigator, Co-PI or investigator, including a randomised trial on adjuvant temozolomide with or without interferon alfa in high-grade gliomas published in JAMA Network Open.

items.question: Does Prof. Zhong-Ping Chen accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to brain tumours at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Chen's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Chen specialises in microsurgery and multimodality treatment for gliomas and other primary and metastatic brain tumours.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is Prof. Chen involved in clinical trials for glioma?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Chen has participated in more than 20 clinical trials for glioma treatment over the past 20 years, including a randomised trial on adjuvant temozolomide published in JAMA Network Open.

items.question: What is Prof. Chen known for in glioma research?
items.answer: Prof. Chen was the first to identify vasculogenic mimicry, a novel form of tumour circulation, in malignant gliomas, and has investigated cell-based immunotherapy approaches including CIK cells and dendritic cell-glioma fusion cells.
